sample_unit: elderly residents (with four nurses, three rooms, seven days)

links.outcome: Alarm load reduction to nurses by context-aware filtering versus notifying all nurses
links.effect: Average alarm load reduced to 27.5% (72.5% reduction) versus 100% baseline; macro F1 0.18 to 0.97; FPR 0.20 to 0.005; FNR 0.79 to 0.023.
links.quote: Compared to the baseline where all nurses were notified (100% alarm load), the proposed method reduced average alarm load to 27.5%, achieving a 72.5% reduction, with suppression rates reaching 100% in some rooms for some nurses.

unlisted_practices: Hybrid LLM plus rule-based context-aware alert suppression, delay, and validation using nurse-resident proximity and care level

screen.reason: The study deployed and evaluated a hybrid LLM and rule-based system in a real-world long-term care setting to suppress, delay, and validate nurse alerts, directly measuring alarm load reduction and alarm fatigue mitigation against a baseline alerting strategy.
